name: Rabat
subtitle: Rabat, capital of Morocco: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 509,916 people live in the city of Rabat (counted 2024), within an urban conurbation of over 1.8 million.
Rabat was founded in 1150 by Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min as a ribat overlooking the Bou Regreg and the Atlantic.
Rabat was chosen as administrative capital in 1912 under the French protectorate and reaffirmed as capital upon independence in 1956.

parts.text: Rabat was established in 1150 by Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min as a fortified ribat on a high coastal promontory, expanded at the end of the 12th century by Caliph Abu Yaqub Yusuf al-Mansur with monumental walls and gates.

In 1912 General Hubert Lyautey made Rabat the administrative capital of the French Protectorate in Morocco. Urban planners designed a new town with wide boulevards and public gardens while deliberately conserving the historic Medina and Kasbah.
Upon recovering national independence in March 1956, King Mohammed V retained Rabat as the permanent sovereign capital of Morocco.

parts.text: 509,916 in September 2024, according to the official national census (RGPH 2024) conducted by the Haut-Commissariat au Plan. The Rabat Prefecture counted 515,619 residents, while the metropolitan area shared with twin city Salé across the Bou Regreg exceeds 1.8 million.

items.text: Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min builds the original ribat (Kasbah des Oudayas).
Abu Yaqub Yusuf al-Mansur expands the city walls and begins the Hassan Mosque and minaret.
The Marinid dynasty develops the Chellah necropolis with a mosque, madrasa and royal tombs.
Rabat is designated the administrative capital of the French Protectorate in Morocco.
Morocco recovers independence; Rabat is confirmed as the sovereign national capital.
The Mausoleum of Mohammed V, designed by architect Eric Vo Toan, is completed facing the Hassan Tower.
UNESCO inscribes Rabat on the World Heritage List as a modern capital and historic city.
The Musée Mohammed VI d'art moderne et contemporain opens in central Rabat.
